### Problem: Valid Anagram {#sec-lts-p4-b}

::: {.p-statement}

Given strings `s` and `t` ($1 \le |s|, |t| \le 5 \cdot 10^4$; lowercase English letters), return `true` iff `t` is a reordering of `s` — same characters, same multiplicities. Follow-up asks what changes for Unicode input.

Source: [LC 242 · Valid Anagram](https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-anagram/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}

Example — `s = "anagram", t = "nagaram"`. Output `true`. (`"rat"`/`"car"` → `false`.)
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Two strings are anagrams exactly when their character *multisets* are equal. The cheap test is to canonicalise both by sorting and compare — $O(n \log n)$ comparisons. But the alphabet is fixed at 26, so a 26-slot histogram captures the whole multiset: add for `s`, subtract for `t`, and check every slot returned to zero. That is $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space, and no comparison sort — the counting idea of @sec-lts-a1 turned into an equality test.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Sort and compare.** `sorted(s) == sorted(t)`. $O(n \log n)$ time, $O(n)$ space — the oracle, and a one-liner.
2. **Single histogram.** If the lengths differ, stop (false). Otherwise one 26-array: `cnt[ord(a)-97] += 1` and `cnt[ord(b)-97] -= 1` in one pass; the strings match iff every entry is `0`. $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space.

**Invariant.** After processing the prefixes `s[:i]`, `t[:i]`, each slot holds (count in `s`) minus (count in `t`); it is all-zero at the end iff the two multisets are identical, which for equal lengths is exactly the anagram condition.
:::

The buttons are in order: canonicalise with a comparison sort, then replace it with a fixed-width histogram.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Sort both

::: {.form-next}
Sort the characters of each string and compare the results. $O(n \log n)$ time, $O(n)$ space — obviously correct and the baseline.

**Worked example.** `anagram` → `aaagmnr`, `nagaram` → `aaagmnr`; equal → `true`.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("ana", "sort")
    assert str(final) == "True"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def va242_sort(s, t):
    return sorted(s) == sorted(t)
```

##### C++

```cpp
// canonicalise both by sorting, then compare
bool va242Sort(string s, string t) {
    sort(s.begin(), s.end());
    sort(t.begin(), t.end());
    return s == t;
}
```
:::

**Reading it line by line.** Once sorted, two anagrams are byte-identical, so the equality check is the whole proof. The cost is two comparison sorts, $O(n \log n)$, plus $O(n)$ scratch per string — unavoidable if you insist on the *words* being equal, but the histogram only needs the *counts* to be equal.

#### Histogram (linear, O(1) space)

::: {.form-next}
Guard on equal length, then sweep both strings at once adding for `s` and subtracting for `t` in one 26-slot array; true iff every slot is back to `0`. $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space.

**Worked example.** net counts for `a,n,g,r,a,m,a` vs `n,a,g,a,r,a,m` are all `0` → `true`.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("ana", "count")
    assert str(final) == "True"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-lts-242-count
def va242_count(s, t):
    if len(s) != len(t):
        return False
    cnt = [0] * 26
    for a, b in zip(s, t):
        cnt[ord(a) - 97] += 1
        cnt[ord(b) - 97] -= 1
    return all(c == 0 for c in cnt)

for _ in range(300):
    a = "".join(random.choice("abcde") for _ in range(random.randint(1, 20)))
    lst = list(a); random.shuffle(lst)
    b = "".join(lst)
    assert va242_count(a, b) is True
    assert va242_count(a, b) == va242_sort(a, b)
    c = a + "z"
    assert va242_count(a, c) is False
assert va242_count("anagram", "nagaram") is True
assert va242_count("rat", "car") is False
assert va242_count("ab", "a") is False
print("va242_count OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
// one shared 26-counter, net to zero iff anagrams
bool va242Count(string s, string t) {
    if (s.size() != t.size()) return false;
    vector<int> cnt(26, 0);
    for (size_t i = 0; i < s.size(); ++i) {
        ++cnt[s[i] - 'a'];
        --cnt[t[i] - 'a'];
    }
    for (int c : cnt) if (c != 0) return false;
    return true;
}
```
:::

**Reading it line by line.** The `len` guard lets the single `zip` loop be safe and turns a length mismatch into an instant `false`. Because we add and subtract into the *same* array, we never store two histograms — the space is the fixed 26 slots regardless of `n`, which is why this beats the sort on both axes. The stress test shuffles `a` into `b` (guaranteeing anagrams), confirms `a` vs `a+"z"` is false, and cross-checks against `va242_sort`.
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Sort** is $O(n \log n)$ time, $O(n)$ space. **Histogram** is $O(n)$ time, $O(1)$ space (26 slots). For Unicode, swap the fixed array for a hash map keyed by code point — $O(n)$ time, $O(A)$ space where $A$ is the distinct-symbol count.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Different lengths can never be anagrams — the guard rejects before any counting.
- Repeated letters (`"aa"`, `"aa"`) net to zero on slot `a`; multiplicity is honoured.
- Empty input is excluded by $|s| \ge 1$, but the code would return `true` for two empty strings.
:::
